title: King of Zugzwang: Punish the Queen Retreat
summary: A queen can block its own king’s flight while a knight and bishop cover the remaining exits.

nodes.question: Why does the queen retreat to b7 fail?
nodes.explanation: Bg4 checks along g4–f5–e6–d7–c8. Nc6 covers b8 and d8, while Black’s queen and pawn fill b7 and c7.

branches.title: Conditional source mate after Qb7
commentary: Begin after Qb7 in the earlier diagram, with Black’s pawn still on a5. The later a4 diagram is a different position; no full zugzwang proof is asserted here.

Bg4# checks Kc8 along the long diagonal and covers d7. Nc6 controls b8/d8, Black’s own Qb7/c7 occupy the other flights, and Qb7 cannot capture the bishop or block on d7/e6/f5. The king has no legal reply.

exercises.prompt: Why does the queen fail to defend its king?
exercises.answer: On b7 it occupies a flight square but cannot capture Bg4 or reach an interposition square on g4–c8.

exercises.prompt: Does this certify the entire zugzwang?
exercises.answer: No. It proves the immediate mate after Qb7 only. The later queen confinement, waiting move and complete minor-piece conversion remain outside this proof.
